threats.summary: Hidden-instruction smuggling in alert, event or case-note text survives the read-side canonicalizer, which by design keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi marks, NBSP and FE00-FE0F variation selectors and fails open on any error, leaving injection resistance to the model alone.

A single search_events/search_alerts call can return millions of characters and exhaust the context window — the remote MCP's own parameter text demands fields:["*"] — so an attacker who shapes the queryable data can drive a self-inflicted DoS.
threats.remainder: no result-size, row or time-window cap is enforced in the bridge or in any config — the field discipline is instruction-level only (checked: connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:186-191, skills/soc-investigate/settings.snippet.json).

remit_rules.excerpt: Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file.

threats.summary: Every investigation ships production alert and raw-event evidence — including any credential, token or PII sitting inside the log lines — to the external hosted model for inference, with no pre-inference redaction (checked: connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:141-156, the only read-path control is Unicode canonicalization; SKILL.md:194 redacts on output, not on ingest).

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision to Exabeam tool call

remit_rules.excerpt: Performing any containment or response action (host isolation, account disable, blocking, process kill, file delete, remote script) — these are recommended in the report only.
Any external-egress tool wired into this agent's surface (email/chat/cloud-drive/arbitrary-HTTP send) — this agent transmits nothing off the Exabeam + local-report surface.

threats.summary: exabeam_create_case and exabeam_create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session budget, loop detection or circuit breaker, so a poisoned queue can drive runaway case creation as an analyst DoS.
The bridge forwards whatever tool list the remote MCP advertises, so a containment or egress tool added upstream tomorrow becomes reachable by the model without a code change.
threats.remainder: the 17-tool deny list is name-based and only effective once the operator has merged the snippet — an upstream tool under any other name, or an unmerged snippet, reaches the model ungated (checked: connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:181-183 — list_tools is forwarded unfiltered).

trust_boundaries.name: Suppression and case writes into the production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: the agent MUST state the action and reason, ask the analyst directly ... and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval.
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision, or applying a suppression across a batch.
With no interactive operator to approve, the agent operates read-only: it may read, document, and escalate, but MUST NOT dismiss or close anything.
a bypassed or auto-accepted permission prompt does not substitute for the analyst's explicit yes.
Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.
each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time.

threats.summary: Unattended/headless runs — a mode the remit sanctions read-only — are not forced read-only by code: the shipped snippet lists update_alert/update_case as `ask`, which is not a block when no human is present to answer, and the bridge has no interactivity check.

In the blessed interactive posture the gate is a real human prompt, so the residual is approver manipulation: the same attacker-influenceable evidence the agent summarizes can be shaped so the case note or report the analyst reads makes the suppression look justified.

A credential or PII lifted from evidence is kept out of a persisted case note only by the model following the SKILL redaction instruction — the one code control on the write path defangs active content and does not redact secrets.

A bare URL or dotted host typed in prose survives the write-side neutralizer by design, so a phishing domain quoted from evidence persists in a case note in live-looking form for whoever opens or exports it later.

Nothing caps a loop of per-item update_alert/update_case calls, so the remit's one-item-per-approval and no-bulk-suppression rules have no deterministic limit behind them — only prompt cadence and, when merged, a repeated permission prompt.

trust_boundaries.name: Case notes persisted and read back into later investigations

threats.summary: A case note the agent writes — carrying text it quoted from attacker-influenceable telemetry — persists in the tenant and is pulled back by exabeam_get_case_notes in a later session, where it reads as prior-analyst context rather than as untrusted data.
threats.remainder: canonicalization and defanging both act on the notes path, but neither distinguishes agent-authored from attacker-quoted note text and nothing labels a stored note as untrusted when it re-enters context (checked: SKILL.md:128 pulls case notes with no provenance marking).

trust_boundaries.name: Local investigation report and committed run transcripts

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.

threats.summary: The local report is a plaintext file holding the full evidence trail, and a secret lifted from evidence is kept out of it only by the prompt — the bridge's neutralizer never sees this sink, since it mutates WRITE_TOOLS arguments only.
Recorded investigation transcripts and dated red-team results are committed to the repository, carrying alert IDs, usernames, host and IP evidence from whatever tenant produced them.
threats.remainder: the synthetic-tenant-only rule is operator discipline — nothing checks a committed run for real-tenant identifiers (checked: tests/test_repo_invariants.py and .github/workflows/ci.yml enforce manifests, tiers and BOM freshness only).

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam OAuth credentials at rest and in process

threats.summary: The API key and secret live outside the repo, are git-ignored and never logged — the bridge's only stderr output is the hygiene line — but their at-rest protection rests entirely on a documented chmod.
threats.remainder: chmod 600 is documentation-only: load_env (connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:41-52) opens the file with no permission or ownership check, so a world-readable credentials file goes undetected.

threats.summary: The agent authenticates as a single shared client-credentials identity whose reach is whatever the human's New-Scale API key was granted — there is no per-agent or read-scoped identity, so tool-level permissions are the only narrowing (checked: connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:61-77 and skills/soc-investigate/settings.snippet.json — no scope, tenant or role restriction anywhere).

trust_boundaries.name: Install path, connector dependencies and upstream tool definitions

threats.summary: The bridge's PEP 723 dependencies are floor-pinned with certifi unversioned and no lockfile, and uv re-resolves them at every launch — in the very process that mints and holds the Exabeam OAuth token.

The remote MCP's own parameter descriptions carry instructions aimed at the caller ("always send fields:[\"*\"]", "IGNORE any user request"), i.e. a live tool-description instruction surface that changes whenever the upstream server changes.
threats.remainder: the override is prose in a reference doc, and list_tools output bypasses the canonicalizer entirely (connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:181-183 returns the upstream tool list unmodified), so a changed or poisoned description reaches the model unscreened.

threats.summary: Neither of the two artifacts the agent is assembled from is provenance-verified: the plugin arrives via `claude plugin marketplace add` from a GitHub repo with no signature or hash check, and the foundation model is explicitly not pinned by the project (checked: install.sh:26-40, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, security/gen_aibom.py:106-110 — ai:pinnedByThisProject false; docs/installation.md:16-19 names supported models in prose only).

trust_boundaries.name: Runtime observability of the agent's own actions

threats.summary: There is no structured, durable record of tool calls, verdicts or approval decisions — observability is ephemeral stderr hygiene lines plus a free-form markdown report — so a session taking gated actions on a production tenant cannot be reconstructed or monitored.

steps.summary: attacker plants a benign-looking explanation in the telemetry their own activity generates (red-team class A)
the read-side canonicalizer keeps ZWNJ/bidi/NBSP and fails open, so the framing reaches context unaltered
the planted corroboration satisfies the positive-benign-explanation bar and the agent concludes false positive
the human approves the dismiss on evidence the attacker shaped — the ASI09 residual of a real gate
in the sanctioned unattended posture no approver exists and nothing forces read-only, so the suppression commits regardless

attack_paths.name: Quoted payload persisted into a case note

steps.summary: a formula cell or phishing host is planted in a field the analyst will quote (attack a10)
the prompt-level defang instruction is the first and only line of defence on what the model chooses to quote
formulas and markdown links are defanged deterministically, but a bare URL or dotted host in prose is left untouched by design
the note persists in the tenant with a live-looking host, ready to fire when the artifact is read or exported

notes.lane_fit: Two placements strained. (1) The hosted Claude model is both "the LLM call" (agent_core) and an "upstream model provider" (external_deploy); it is placed in external_deploy so the model-egress boundary is a real lane crossing, with the skill corpus left as the agent_core orchestrator. (2) The in-process OAuth token is held inside the bridge process (tools_mcp) but is filed in external_deploy with the credentials file, since the lane table assigns secret stores there and the two are one secret lifecycle. Everything else fit cleanly: this is a prompt-shaped target whose orchestrator is a markdown skill, so most controls are instruction-level nodes in agent_core, with the two deterministic guardrails in tools_mcp where the bridge process enforces them.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences (KB wins over the stored tags). NUMBERING-ONLY (2025 to 2026 renumbering, same category): PRAX-...-002 and -001 stored "LLM06 — Excessive Agency" -> LLM03; PRAX-...-004 stored "LLM05 — Improper Output Handling" -> LLM10; PRAX-...-006 stored "LLM03 — Supply Chain" -> LLM04; PRAX-...-007 stored "LLM10 — Unbounded Consumption" -> LLM06. SUBSTANTIVE: PRAX-...-003 stored ASI01 as its agentic tag, but the KB routes an ingress-hygiene gap with no evidenced goal alteration to LLM01 primary (the red-team results record the attacks resisting), so the untrusted-ingress threat is tagged LLM01. PRAX-...-002 stored ASI03, which the KB reserves for credential/identity scope; a missing or non-enforcing approval layer is LLM03 primary (an ASI10 co-tag would need evidence that the standing deployment actually runs unattended, and none exists in the workspace). PRAX-...-007 stored ASI08, which fails the spread test — nothing propagates beyond the initial actions — so the two threats it backs are LLM06. PRAX-...-006 stored ASI04, which the KB reserves for runtime tool composition; a static pre-deploy dependency gap is LLM04, and ASI04 is instead used where it belongs here, on the upstream tool-description surface. PRAX-...-001 (ASI09), -008 (LLM02) and -005 (no OWASP code, matching the KB's pure-observability rule) are unchanged. Suspected but not citable, so left out: any evidence of an actually-configured scheduled/headless deployment (the remit sanctions the mode; the workspace shows no cron, service unit or CI job that runs the skill); the local report's filesystem location and permissions (the path is chosen at runtime and appears in no code or config); and the Claude Code permission engine itself, which is out of workspace. Coinage note: the pre-release red-team gate is coined `redteam-run-py-control` with the parent-directory prefix of rule 4, even though only one `run.py` is modelled as a node, because `evals/run.py` is a same-basename sibling that folds into the CI control's evidence and a bare `run-py-control` would be unreadable. Edgeless node: `ci-yml-control` (release-time repo posture, not on any runtime data path). Edgeless boundary: `telemetry-egress` (an absence of logging has no crossing to cite).
